LXX: Let all the nations arise and go up into the valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations round about; send forth the sickles, for the vintage is at hand. Come in and tread, for the winepress is full and the vats overflow, for their evils are filled up. These things too they interpret in two ways, following the sense given above. […]

3:14.t: Peoples, peoples in the valley of cutting down, for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of cutting down. The sun and the moon have been darkened, and the stars have withdrawn their brightness. LXX: Sounds have been heard in the valley of judgment, for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of judgment. The sun and the moon will be darkened, and the stars will make their brightness set. In the place where we have put peoples, peoples, and the Seventy translated sounds have been heard, in the Hebrew is written amonim, amonim, which certainly signifies the multitude and the crowds of those who are to be judged, not noise and sound. Again, where we said in the valley of cutting down, following the translation of Aquila and Symmachus and the Fifth edition, the Seventy and Theodotion translated τῆς δίκης καί τῆς κρίσεως, that is, of the case and of judgment; […]

3:15.t: The grief of that day and the torments of those who perish not even the sun and moon and the other stars will be able to look upon, but they will withdraw their brightness, and will not dare to behold the severity of him who judges and renders each one's work upon his own head. Not that they are more merciful than the judgments of God, but that every creature, at the torments of others, trembles for its own judgment.

3:16.t: And the Lord will roar from Zion, and from Jerusalem he will utter his voice, and the heavens and the earth will be moved; and the Lord is the hope of his people and the strength of the sons of Israel; and you will know that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain; and Jerusalem will be holy, and strangers will not pass through her any more. LXX: But the Lord will cry out from Zion, and from Jerusalem he will utter his voice, and heaven and earth will be moved; and the Lord will spare his people, and will strengthen the sons of Israel; and you will know that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain; and Jerusalem will be holy, and the foreigner will not pass through her any more. When the brightness of the sun and moon and all the stars has been changed into darkness, the Lord will roar from Zion like a lion, or cry out; and his voice will be so loud and terrible that the hinges of the heavens and the foundations of the earth will be shaken. […]

3:17.t: Then both those who will be punished and those who will be taken up into glory will know that the Lord dwells in his watchtower Zion, and in Christ, his holy mountain, or in him who has prepared himself as a worthy dwelling place of God. Then Jerusalem, the vision of peace, will be holy, from which Solomon too received his name, and strangers will not pass through her any more. Understand by strangers either the demons, who are alien to God, or all the worst thoughts and sins, of which the prophet speaks: From strangers spare your servant; which would by no means find a way into us any more, if we have the peace of God and our heart has not lain open to the adversaries. These things the Jews and, as we have said, our Judaizers refer to the fable of the thousand years, when they think that Christ will dwell in Zion, and that the peoples of the saints will be gathered into a Jerusalem of gold and gems, so that those who in this age have been oppressed by all the nations may in this same age rule over all the nations.

3:18.t: Blessed is he from whom Jesus asks drink, as He did from that Samaritan woman, and gives a well of water springing up unto eternal life. Blessed is he that soweth beside all waters, and upon every soul, tomorrow to be ploughed and watered, which today the ox and the ass tread, while it is dry and without water, and oppressed with unreason. And blessed is he who, though he be a "valley of rushes," is watered out of the House of the Lord; for he is made fruitbearing instead of rushbearing, and produces that which is for the food of man, not that which is rough and unprofitable. And for the sake of this we must be very careful not to miss the Grace.

And it will be in that day: the mountains will drip sweetness, and the hills will flow with milk, and through all the streams of Judah waters will go. LXX: And it will be in that day: the mountains will drip sweetness, and the hills will flow with milk, and all the outlets of Judah will flow with waters. When the Lord dwells in Zion and on his holy mountain, when no one will attempt to pass through holy Jerusalem, whoever in her is a mountain, and has reached the heights of the virtues, will sweat sweetness and honey; and from him will drip spiritual graces, of which the prophet speaks: How sweet are your words to my throat, above honey to my mouth. But he who is lower than the mountains, and has not yet climbed to the summit of perfection, will be called a hill, and from him will flow streams of milk, by which the untaught infancy in Christ is nourished, and the rivers of water which the Lord testified would flow from his belly. […]

For the flocks of the believers have, as it were, a pasture full of divers plants and flowers, in the holy Scriptures, which are their wise guides: and filled with spiritual joy at the glorious doctrines and instructions which they contain, they frequent the sacred courts. And this it is which long ago was proclaimed in the words of Isaiah: "And there shall be upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill, running waters upon that day." And again; "And the mountains shall drop sweetness: and the hills flow with milk." For it is the custom of divine Scripture to compare to mountains and hills those set over others, and whose office it is to teach, inasmuch as they are high exalted, in respect, I mean, of their thoughts being occupied with elevated subjects, and withdrawn from things earthly: while the waters and the sweetness and the milk are the instructions which flow from them as from fountains. […]
3:18.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

3:19.t: Egypt will be a desolation, and Idumea a desert of perdition, because they have acted wickedly against the sons of Judah, and have shed innocent blood in their land. LXX: Egypt will be in perdition, and Idumea a plain of desolation, because of the iniquities of the sons of Judah, because they have shed righteous blood in their land. In this place too the Jews sleep a very heavy sleep, imagining with a most vain hope that in the last time, when they are to receive not Christ but the Antichrist, there will be vengeance for them upon the Egyptians, who are their neighbors, and upon the Romans, whom they interpret as the Idumeans: namely, that just as Pharaoh and all his army, who held the people of God captive for four hundred and thirty years, were drowned in the Red Sea, so also the Romans, who are to possess the Jews for the same span of years, may be destroyed by the vengeance of the Lord. Let them promise themselves this with an empty hope. […]

3:20.t: And Judea will be inhabited for ever, and Jerusalem to generation and generation; and I will cleanse their blood, which I had not cleansed; and the Lord will abide in Zion. LXX: But Judea will be inhabited for ever, and Jerusalem to generations of generations; and I will seek out their blood, and will not suffer it to be unavenged. And the Lord will dwell in Zion. Surely it is not this Judea that will be inhabited for ever, which we see to be deserted, nor this Jerusalem, whose ruins we behold, but that Judea whose daughters have exulted and rejoiced in all the judgments of the Lord, and of which we read at the end of the fiftieth (51st) psalm: Deal kindly, O Lord, in your good will with Zion, that the walls of Jerusalem may be built. […]

3:21.t: And the Lord will cleanse the blood of all sins, which he had not cleansed before, so as to cleanse in the Gospel those whom, sinning under the law, he had left unclean. For he has shut up all things under sin for this purpose, that he may have mercy on all; or he will avenge the blood of his servants, which they have shed in martyrdom for the confession of his name. And the Lord will abide in Zion, of which it is written: Its foundations are on the holy mountains; the Lord loves the gates of Zion above all the tents of Jacob.
